interactions.label: Gaussian radius r
interactions.teaches: A Gaussian cylinder placed anywhere in the insulating gap encloses the same positive inner-conductor charge, while its area grows as 2πrL, so the field magnitude varies as 1/r.

interactions.label: Build the Gauss-law setup
interactions.teaches: The capacitance derivation depends on matching the enclosed charge, the chosen cylindrical Gaussian surface, and the radial electric field crossing only the curved side area.
Rotating the scene makes clear that the dashed curve is a full coaxial cylinder nested between two conducting cylinders, not a flat circle drawn on the end face.

demo_steps.title: Charges on the conductors
demo_steps.narration: The inner conductor carries positive charge and the outer shell carries negative charge. The red field arrows point radially outward only through the annular gap between the conductors.

demo_steps.title: Choose a Gaussian cylinder in the gap
demo_steps.narration: The dashed orange cylinder is placed at radius r with R1 < r < R2. It encloses the positive charge on the inner cylinder but not the negative charge on the outer conductor.

demo_steps.title: Move r outward
demo_steps.narration: Increasing r keeps the enclosed charge the same, but increases the curved area 2πrL. The field arrows shorten, showing E(r) = λ/(2πε0r).

plan.geometry_notes: Use a long coaxial capacitor aligned approximately along world X, with the near end at x = -3.5 and the far end at x = +3.5. In the default camera, the cylinder should appear stretched mostly horizontally, slanting slightly from lower-left near end to upper-right far end. Length L ≈ 7.0 units. Inner conductor radius R1 = 0.55 units. Outer conductor inner radius R2 = 1.75 units. Outer conductor outer radius ≈ 2.0 units. The Gaussian radius slider must remain strictly in the annular gap: 0.65 ≤ r ≤ 1.65, never inside the metal and never outside the outer conductor. Outer shell color pale blue #b9c4e6 with opacity 0.28 to 0.35, edge/rim outlines blue-gray #6f7f9f. Inner conductor color blue-gray #9fa8c4 with darker rim #5f6d88. Charge symbols are black #111111; plus signs should crowd the near face of the inner conductor and repeat sparsely along its length, while minus signs should sit on the visible outer shell surface and around the near rim. Electric field arrows should be dark red #b71c1c, thicker and larger than ordinary annotation arrows: shaft length about 0.55 to 0.75 units near default r, shaft radius about 0.025, cone length about 0.14. Draw 10 to 14 radial E arrows in the near-end annulus, distributed all around the inner cylinder face; they originate just outside R1 and point outward toward R2. Scale their visible length roughly proportional to 1/r as gaussianRadius changes, but keep them prominent enough to read. Label E in dark red, enlarged, just left/above the cluster of radial arrows. Gaussian surface should be simplified to match the source: draw only dashed orange #f28c00 end ellipses at x = -3.5 and x = +3.5 plus two main dashed orange longitudinal generator lines along the apparent upper and lower silhouettes. Avoid a translucent filled cylinder except for an optional extremely faint orange surface highlight opacity ≤ 0.04 during the flux stage. Place the label Gaussian surface above the cylinder near the upper middle, with a curved black leader pointing down to the top dashed longitudinal line. At the far right end, draw the radius construction on the end plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Use one common axis point, then three fanning black arrows: R1 shortest to the inner conductor radius, angled slightly up; r intermediate to the orange dashed Gaussian ellipse, angled up-right or outward; R2 longest to the inner surface of the outer shell, angled down-right or farther outward. Enlarge the arrowheads and labels; place labels immediately beyond arrow tips so R1, r, and R2 cannot overlap. Mathematical relation: for R1 < r < R2, q_enc = λL, flux Φ = E(2πrL), and E(r) = λ/(2π ε0 r). The field inside ideal conducting material is zero, but this plan intentionally does not include invalid inner-conductor or outside-conductor radius states because the source figure focuses on the Gaussian surface in the gap.
plan.notes: Use perspective rendering but with a low-elevation, nearly side-on camera so the cylinder reads as a long horizontal cutaway rather than a steep 3D object. Use transparent double-sided cylinder materials and explicit rim curves so the nested radii remain legible. Render dashed Gaussian ellipses and longitudinal lines with LineDashedMaterial or repeated short curve segments; do not add dense surface striping. Keep all labels as screen-facing text sprites anchored to source-like locations. The derivationStage state should change emphasis only: charges stage brightens plus/minus symbols, gaussianSurface stage brightens the orange dashed cylinder and R1/r/R2 arrows, and flux stage subtly highlights the curved Gaussian area while keeping the red radial E arrows prominent. Update the Gaussian ellipses, dashed generator lines, the far-end r arrow, and field-arrow lengths whenever gaussianRadius changes.

authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional cutaway of a cylindrical capacitor drawn in perspective, extending from the near end at the lower left toward the far end at the upper right. Two concentric conducting cylinders share a common axis: a narrow inner cylinder whose visible near face is crowded with plus signs, and a much wider outer shell whose surface carries minus signs spaced along its length and around its near rim. In the near end view, short red arrows labeled 'E' radiate outward from the inner cylinder across the annular gap to the inner wall of the outer shell, filling the gap uniformly in every radial direction. An orange dashed cylinder of intermediate radius is drawn between the two conductors, appearing as dashed ellipses at both ends joined by dashed lines running the length of the device; a curved leader from the top labels it 'Gaussian surface'. At the far end three arrows fan out from a point on the axis, labeled 'R1', 'r', and 'R2' in order of increasing length. Nesting the dashed surface between the two conductor radii shows precisely which charge it encloses. The geometry sets up the flux calculation that gives the capacitance of a coaxial pair carrying charges plus Q and minus Q.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for Gaussian radius r: the learner moves the dashed cylindrical surface from R1 toward R2, the enclosed charge stays on the inner conductor while the radial E arrows at the surface change length, showing why the field in the annular gap depends on r.
- Toggle between conductor, gap, and outside regions: the learner selects a radial zone, the active region highlights and E appears only in the space between cylinders, clarifying where charge is enclosed and where the field vanishes.
authoredContext:
A cylindrical capacitor consists of two concentric, conducting cylinders (the figure). The inner cylinder, of radius R1, may either be a shell or be completely solid. The outer cylinder is a shell of inner radius R2. We assume that the length of each cylinder is l and that the excess charges +Q and −Q reside on the inner and outer cylinders, respectively.

With edge effects ignored, the electrical field between the conductors is directed radially outward from the common axis of the cylinders. Using the Gaussian surface shown in the figure, we have

A cylindrical capacitor consists of two concentric, conducting cylinders. Here, the charge on the outer surface of the inner cylinder is positive (indicated by +) and the charge on the inner surface of the outer cylinder is negative (indicated by −).

Figure shows two concentric cylinders. The inner one, with radius R1 has positive signs on it. The outer one, with radius R2 has negative signs on it. Arrows marked E are shown radiating from the inner one to the outer one. A third cylinder, with radius r, is shown as a dotted line between the two. This is labeled Gaussian surface.

interactions.label: Gaussian radius r
interactions.teaches: Moving the dashed Gaussian cylinder from the inner conductor toward the outer conductor shows that the same enclosed charge is spread over a larger cylindrical area, so the radial electric field in the gap decreases with increasing r.

interactions.label: Radial region
interactions.teaches: Only a Gaussian surface in the annular gap encloses the inner conductor charge without enclosing the compensating outer charge; the electric field vanishes inside conducting material and outside the complete neutral coaxial pair.

demo_steps.title: Inside the gap
demo_steps.narration: The dashed Gaussian cylinder lies between the conductors. It encloses the positive charge on the inner cylinder, so red radial E arrows appear in the annular space.

demo_steps.title: Move r outward
demo_steps.narration: As r approaches the outer cylinder, the enclosed charge is unchanged but the cylindrical area 2πrL grows. The field arrows shorten, matching E = λ/(2πε₀r).

demo_steps.title: Inside a conductor
demo_steps.narration: Selecting the inner conducting region highlights the metal. The electric field is hidden there because electrostatic fields vanish inside a conductor.

demo_steps.title: Outside the capacitor
demo_steps.narration: Outside the outer shell, a Gaussian surface encloses equal and opposite charges, so the net enclosed charge is zero and no external field is drawn.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a coaxial capacitor aligned roughly left-to-right along the world X axis, length L ≈ 6.5 units from x = -3.25 near end to x = +3.25 far end. The visible source view has the near circular end on the left foreground and the far end on the right background; keep the cylinder axis nearly horizontal on screen. Inner conductor radius R1 = 0.55 units, outer conductor inner radius R2 = 1.75 units, outer conductor outer radius ≈ 2.0 units. Gaussian radius r is controlled by the slider and should stay between R1 and R2 in the annular-gap state. Draw the outer shell as a transparent pale blue cylinder, color #b9c4e6 with opacity about 0.35, with darker blue-gray edge outlines #7f8fae. Draw the inner conductor near face as a darker blue-gray disk #a7b0cb, radius 0.55, with a thin red outline at its edge. The annular gap is the space 0.55 < radius < 1.75. Place plus signs in black on the inner cylinder near disk in a compact cluster and along the central tube; place minus signs in black on the outer shell along the upper and lower visible longitudinal surfaces and around both circular rims. Red E arrows #e53935 originate just outside R1 and point radially outward toward R2, mainly on the near-left cross section; arrow lengths should scale approximately as 1/r when the Gaussian radius moves. Orange Gaussian surface is dashed #ff9800: near and far ellipses plus top and bottom longitudinal dashed lines, with opacity 1.0 and no fill or a very faint orange fill below 0.08 opacity if needed. Far-end radius construction should be drawn on the right end plane: three black arrows from the axis, R1 shortest vertical/upward, r intermediate diagonal, R2 longest diagonal/downward or outward, matching the source fan. Formula needed for correctness in the gap: E(r) = λ/(2π ε0 r), flux Φ = E(2πrL), enclosed charge q_enc = λL. In the inner conductor and outside outer conductor states, show E = 0 and hide or gray the red field arrows.
interactionPlan.notes: Use transparent double-sided cylinder materials so the nested coaxial surfaces remain visible. Render dashed Gaussian ellipses as sampled LineDashedMaterial curves in planes perpendicular to the cylinder axis, and render longitudinal dashed lines along the top and bottom apparent silhouette of the Gaussian cylinder. The region toggle should tint the active radial zone: inner conductor light gold for 'Inner conductor', annular gap faint orange for 'Annular gap', and exterior faint gray-blue for 'Outside outer conductor'. Keep text labels screen-facing sprites anchored to their source-like locations. Update Gaussian surface radius, far-end r arrow, and field-arrow lengths reactively on slider changes.

discrepancies: The initial view is much more steeply perspective and foreshortened than the source's side-on textbook projection, making the cylinder look shorter and less like the original composition.
The Gaussian surface is drawn with a faint translucent/striped cylinder and full end loops, whereas the source mainly shows two orange dashed longitudinal generators and dashed end ellipses.
The red electric-field arrows are comparatively faint and sparse; in the source they are bold, prominent radial arrows filling the annular region around the inner conductor.
The right-end R1, r, and R2 construction arrows are crowded and less clearly arranged than in the source, where their radial meanings are visually distinct.
The added region controls introduce states not shown in the source, and the 'Inner conductor'/'Outside outer conductor' settings do not place the Gaussian radius in physically correct regions.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is recognizable as the coaxial Gaussian-surface diagram with correct major elements, but the viewpoint, field-arrow prominence, Gaussian-surface styling, and some interactive region states reduce fidelity and can mislead.
action_items: Adjust the default camera to a more side-on oblique view with the cylinder stretched horizontally like the source.
Make the red radial E arrows darker, larger, and more prominent around the inner conductor.
Simplify the Gaussian surface to match the source more closely: dashed orange end ellipses plus the two main dashed longitudinal lines, with less translucent surface striping.
Reposition and enlarge the R1, r, and R2 labels/arrows on the right end so their meanings are unambiguous.
plan_action_items: Revise the region interaction so 'inner conductor' and 'outside outer conductor' use physically correct radius ranges, or remove those extra states if the goal is strict reproduction of the source figure.

feedback.rationale: The figure is visually close, but the Concept-Misunderstood failure and plan action item identify an incorrect interaction structure with physically wrong region states, requiring plan revision before rendering polish.
